headline:
Firm on who,
loose on how.
intro: I keep one map of the team. Along with who owns what and who people turn to for help, it tracks where each person wants to grow, which is the part most org charts leave out. Staffing and funding asks come from that map, so people get growth they chose and the company gets a design group that helps set the plan.

levels.label: Person
levels.imageAlt: A person sits within concentric map guides, connected to product and specialty tags, with an outward arrow marking their chosen growth direction.

principles.headline:
Ownership people
can find.
principles.body: Product partners should know which designer to call, and designers should know which teammate to ask. I shape ownership around how the company already works so both answers are obvious.

principles.headline:
Goals they wrote,
tied to yours.
principles.body: Each quarter we write personal goals against what the business needs. I assign work to match, so growth and delivery follow the same plan.

principles.headline:
I coach judgment,
not process.
principles.body: Most of our 1:1 time goes to the moments when a partner is stuck and the next move isn’t obvious. That judgment looks different on every team.

levels.label: Team
levels.imageAlt: Six peers sit within overlapping circular map guides and exchange work along neighboring arrows, with no central manager node.

principles.headline:
Problems route
sideways first.
principles.body: Specialties help the team answer most questions together. That keeps me out of the critical path and makes it clear who the senior people are.

principles.headline:
The team owns
the quality bar.
principles.body: A weekly roundtable and design review decides what we improve and who leads it, so standards hold whether or not I’m in the room.

principles.headline:
Stuck work gets a
second pair of hands.
principles.body: When something stalls I work alongside the designer. They keep ownership of the project, build their judgment, and need less of me the next time.

levels.label: Company
levels.imageAlt: An arrow leads into a shared map of products and designers, where two marks show gaps in design coverage.

principles.headline:
The customer gets
a seat at the table.
principles.body: Product brings the business case and engineering brings what’s feasible to build. Design brings what customers need, and I make sure that carries equal weight when we decide what to build.

principles.headline:
Name the gaps
out loud.
principles.body: Some products won’t have a designer. I make the cost visible in customer and business terms, so staffing is a decision we make together instead of a quiet backlog.

principles.headline:
Team shape is
a design decision.
principles.body: Structure shapes retention and the quality of the work, so I design it with the leaders it serves.

closing.statement: The map is the one constant.
closing.note: Each company gets its own version, and the work changes with it.
